summary.title: ios playbook
summary.description:
STRIDE threat model of the external iOS playbook (playbooks/ios-platform-feature-*.md). 
One diagram per platform-feature risk; threats map to the playbook risks and their mitigations to the playbook controls.

data.name: Apple App Store
data.description: Apple servers that deliver the current production package of the target app to any Apple ID that holds the app licence.

data.name: Target app
data.description: Target app installed on a physical iPhone signed in to the same Apple ID as the macOS workstation.

threats.title: Obfuscated secrets recovered at runtime
threats.description: Obfuscation from Swift Confidential prevents easy static extraction, but secrets are de-obfuscated in memory when used. An attacker can still recover them at runtime through hooking, memory dumping or patching.
threats.mitigation: Treat client-side secrets as recoverable: avoid shipping long-lived secrets in the app where possible, and add runtime integrity / anti-tampering checks to raise the cost of runtime attacks.

data.name: Apple Configurator
data.description: Apple Configurator on macOS. Adding the target app from the Apps tab downloads the production IPA and caches it locally.

data.name: Configurator cache
data.description: ~/Library/Group Containers/K36BKF7T3D.group.com.apple.configurator/Library/Caches/Assets/TemporaryItems/MobileApps/ - temporary copy of the downloaded .ipa.

data.name: Extracted IPA
data.description: Copy of the .ipa in the analysis workspace: app executable, Info.plist and bundled .plist / resource files.

threats.title: Hardcoded secrets extracted from the app binary
threats.description: Static analysis of the IPA (e.g. MobSF) recovers plaintext literals compiled into the executable, such as hardcoded credentials, API keys, URLs and configuration values. MITRE ATT&CK: Discovery (TA0032). Playbook: playbooks/ios-platform-feature-01-risk-01.md
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-01-risk-01-control-01 - Obfuscate plaintext literals: move sensitive literals to confidential.yml (not bundled), let the Swift Confidential build plugin generate obfuscated accessors (Secrets.$apiKey), then re-scan the rebuilt IPA with MobSF to verify the literals are no longer recoverable.

threats.title: Credentials exposed in bundled .plist resources
threats.description: App resources such as bundled .plist files are extracted directly from the IPA, exposing plaintext usernames, passwords and other configuration values.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-01-risk-01-control-02 - Remove plaintext literals from bundled .plist files; replace stored credentials with salted SHA-256 hashes and compare hash(input + salt) at authentication; re-run MobSF to confirm no plaintext literals remain.

data.name: MobSF
data.description: Mobile Security Framework static analyser used to score the app and surface hardcoded keys, embedded URLs and other exposed data.

data.name: Attacker
data.description: Adversary (or authorised tester) with an Apple ID that holds the app licence and a macOS workstation.

data.name: Production IPA download
data.description: Apple Configurator downloads the current production package using the Apple ID app licence.

threats.title: Production IPA obtainable by any licensed Apple ID
threats.description: Platform behaviour (ios-platform-feature-01): any user with the app licence can obtain the production IPA through Apple Configurator. This cannot be prevented by the app; the model assumes the attacker holds the IPA.
threats.mitigation: Accepted platform behaviour - design the app assuming its package is public. See the controls on the Extracted IPA store.

data.name: USB pairing + app licence
data.description: iPhone connected over USB, signed in to the same Apple ID so Configurator can access the app licence.

data.name: Writes .ipa
data.description: Downloaded package temporarily stored in the local cache.

data.name: Copy .ipa
data.description: Attacker copies the .ipa from the cache to the analysis workspace using Terminal.

data.name: Upload .ipa
data.description: IPA uploaded to MobSF for static analysis.

data.name: Findings report
data.description: Report listing hardcoded keys, embedded URLs, possible credentials and configuration issues.

data.name: Target app
data.description: Target app on the iPhone; Wi-Fi is configured with a manual proxy pointing at the workstation on port 8080.

threats.title: Interception proxy accepted as the backend
threats.description: Because the Burp CA is fully trusted on the device and the app does not pin, the app accepts Burp-issued certificates as the backend's identity.
threats.mitigation: Implement certificate or public-key pinning for backend connections (the playbook notes pinned apps reject Burp certificates). Complement with ios-platform-feature-02-risk-01-control-01 proxy detection.

data.name: iOS trust store
data.description: Device certificate trust settings. Burp Suite CA profile installed and enabled under Certificate Trust Settings.

threats.title: User-installed interception CA is fully trusted
threats.description: Installing and trusting the Burp CA is a test prerequisite, not itself a vulnerability (see playbooks/ios-platform-feature-02-risk-01.md). It is recorded here to make the assumption explicit.
threats.mitigation: No app-side control; the risk is realised only when the app does not pin certificates.

data.name: Burp Suite proxy
data.description: Burp Suite proxy listener on port 8080 bound to all interfaces (or the Mac's local IP), terminating and re-establishing TLS.

data.name: Burp HTTP history
data.description: Proxy > HTTP history containing decrypted requests and responses.

data.name: App backend API
data.description: Backend endpoints the target app communicates with over HTTPS.

data.name: Attacker
data.description: Adversary (or authorised tester) on the same Wi-Fi network who controls the proxy and installed the CA on the device.

data.name: HTTPS via Wi-Fi proxy
data.description: App requests routed to Burp through the manual Wi-Fi proxy and decrypted with the Burp CA.

threats.title: HTTPS traffic decrypted by a trusted interception CA
threats.description: App HTTPS traffic is routed through a locally trusted interception proxy and visible in decrypted form, exposing endpoints, tokens and personal data. A finding means no effective pinning was observed for that exchange; it does not mean HTTPS is broken. MITRE ATT&CK: Collection (TA0035). Playbook: playbooks/ios-platform-feature-02-risk-01.md
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-02-risk-01-control-01 - Detect HTTPS traffic proxying: call CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings() and check HTTPEnable, HTTPSEnable and ProxyAutoConfigEnable; if any is enabled, warn the user, log an alert or stop the request. Add certificate pinning so a trusted interception CA alone is not enough.

data.name: Re-encrypted HTTPS
data.description: Burp forwards the (possibly modified) request to the real backend.

threats.title: Requests modified in transit by the proxy
threats.description: An intermediary that can decrypt traffic can also modify requests and responses before forwarding them.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-02-risk-01-control-01 - detect a configured proxy and stop sensitive requests; certificate pinning; validate all requests server-side.

data.name: Responses
data.description: Backend responses returned to the proxy.

data.name: Responses (Burp-issued cert)
data.description: Responses delivered to the app over a TLS session terminated by Burp.

data.name: CA trust decision
data.description: Device trust evaluation accepts certificates issued by the Burp CA.

data.name: Decrypted traffic logged
data.description: Decrypted requests and responses recorded in HTTP history.

data.name: Review traffic
data.description: Attacker reviews endpoints and sensitive data in HTTP history.

data.name: Install + trust Burp CA
data.description: CA downloaded from http://burp/, installed as a profile and enabled for full trust.

data.name: User
data.description: Legitimate user entering or viewing sensitive information in the target app.

data.name: Target app UI
data.description: Target app screens that display or accept usernames, email addresses, passwords and other PII.

threats.title: On-screen PII outside secure fields remains capturable
threats.description: SecureField protects text input fields only. Other sensitive content displayed on screen (usernames, email addresses, account details) can still be captured.
threats.mitigation: Residual risk not covered by the current playbook control. Consider hiding or masking sensitive views while the screen is being captured or mirrored.

data.name: iOS ReplayKit
data.description: System screen capture: screenshots, Control Centre screen recording, broadcast extensions and AirPlay screen mirroring.

data.name: Photos (screenshots)
data.description: Screenshots and screen recordings saved to the Photos library.

threats.title: Sensitive screens saved as screenshots or recordings
threats.description: Volume Up + Side button screenshots or Control Centre recordings store the app interface, including sensitive data, in the Photos library.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-03-risk-01-control-01 - use SecureField for sensitive inputs so their contents are excluded from screenshots and recordings.

data.name: Recorder extension
data.description: feature3-replay_consent_recorder broadcast upload extension; processSampleBuffer appends video frames to a file.

data.name: Recorded video
data.description: Video file written by the recorder app.

data.name: AirPlay receiver
data.description: macOS AirPlay Receiver set to "Allow AirPlay for Everyone" receiving the mirrored iPhone display.

data.name: Attacker
data.description: Adversary who controls the recorder app or AirPlay receiver.

data.name: Enters / views PII
data.description: User enters or views sensitive information.

data.name: Rendered screen frames
data.description: App interface rendered and available to system capture.

data.name: Broadcast video frames
data.description: CMSampleBuffer frames delivered after the user taps Start Broadcast.

threats.title: Sensitive content captured by an authorised screen recording
threats.description: A malicious app with a user-approved broadcast session records the target app's display and collects sensitive information shown on screen. MITRE ATT&CK: Collection (TA0035). Playbook: playbooks/ios-platform-feature-03-risk-01.md
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-03-risk-01-control-01 - Protect sensitive text fields: replace TextField with SecureField for sensitive inputs such as Password so their contents do not appear in screen recordings, screen shares or screenshots.

data.name: Writes video file
data.description: Frames saved to a video file.

data.name: Review recording
data.description: Attacker reviews captured images and video.

data.name: Screenshot / recording
data.description: Screenshot or Control Centre recording saved.

data.name: Screen mirroring
data.description: Control Centre > Screen Mirroring to the macOS workstation.

threats.title: Screen mirrored to an attacker-controlled receiver
threats.description: AirPlay mirroring streams the app display to a macOS receiver where it can be viewed and captured.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-03-risk-01-control-01 - SecureField contents are hidden from screen sharing.

data.name: Capture mirrored display
data.description: Mirrored display viewed and captured on the workstation.

data.name: User
data.description: Legitimate user typing into the target app.

data.name: Custom keyboard
data.description: feature4-localkeyboard extension enabled under Settings > General > Keyboard with Allow Full Access; records each keystroke (KeystrokeStore.append).

threats.title: Keystrokes captured by a third-party keyboard
threats.description: A third-party custom keyboard records sensitive information entered into the target app. MITRE ATT&CK: Collection (TA0035). Playbook: playbooks/ios-platform-feature-04-risk-01.md
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-04-risk-01-control-01 - Protect sensitive text fields: use SecureField for Password, PIN and API key inputs, which forces iOS to use the system keyboard instead of third-party keyboards.

threats.title: Full Access extends keyboard extension capabilities
threats.description: Allow Full Access grants the keyboard extension additional permissions (e.g. network and shared-container access), increasing what it can do with captured input.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-04-risk-01-control-01 keeps sensitive fields on the system keyboard. Residual risk: non-secure fields can still be typed with the custom keyboard.

data.name: KeystrokeStore
data.description: Captured keystrokes retained by the keyboard extension in storage shared with its container app.

threats.title: Captured input retained by the keyboard app
threats.description: Text typed into the target app is persisted and can be viewed later in the keyboard container app.
threats.mitigation: ios-platform-feature-04-risk-01-control-01 - SecureField prevents third-party keyboards from receiving sensitive input in the first place.

data.name: Keyboard app
data.description: Keyboard container app that displays captured inputs.

data.name: Target app fields
data.description: Text fields in the target app (TextField / SecureField).

data.name: System keyboard
data.description: Default iOS keyboard, enforced by iOS for SecureField inputs.

data.name: Attacker
data.description: Developer or operator of the malicious keyboard app.

data.name: Keystrokes
data.description: User types with the custom keyboard selected via the Globe key.

data.name: Inserted text
data.description: Keyboard inserts text into the focused text field.

data.name: Record keystroke
data.description: KeystrokeStore.append(text)

data.name: Read captured input
data.description: Container app reads the captured inputs.

data.name: View captured text
data.description: Captured input viewed by the attacker.

data.name: Secure field input
data.description: For SecureField inputs iOS switches to the system keyboard.

data.name: Text (system keyboard)
data.description: Sensitive input delivered without passing through third-party keyboards.
